public_rationale: The records support that Amazon reported a Fable safeguard bypass before the directive and that jailbreaking was a longstanding, widespread problem. They do not adequately settle the stronger assertion about essentially every contemporary deployed LLM-based system. Stronger defenses are material context, but the absence of a universal jailbreak does not disprove narrower vulnerability. Marcus's hedged impression of panic is not scored or converted into a factual claim about government motives.
limitations: The unresolved verdict concerns the breadth of the technical assertion; the historical component is supported.
Results from older models or bare-model tests cannot automatically establish vulnerability of later deployments with added safeguards.
No numerical meaning is imposed on essentially every.

The factual components are the Amazon bypass report preceding the response, the breadth of practical jailbreak vulnerability, and its established history.
Essentially every ordinarily means almost all major deployed LLM-based systems, allowing exceptions. It does not mean every attack succeeds or that one universal prompt defeats every system.
LLM-based system includes deployed safeguards, not merely the underlying model.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records disprove the factual sequence, or representative contemporary evidence establishes a substantial class of deployed systems resistant to practical jailbreaks. Failure to find a universal jailbreak in one test is insufficient.
